title: From Stochastic to Stable: Rank Stability and Structural Sufficiency in AI Visibility Measurement
abstract: arXiv:2607.10341v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: AI visibility measurement is comparative: practitioners want to know which domains generative search engines cite most often and whether observed differences are large enough to support decisions. Yet the industry lacks a principled way to determine whether enough data has been collected. Collection budgets vary widely across studies and platforms, and conclusions are often drawn from rankings whose stability and precision are unknown. We introduce a sequential convergence framework based on two complementary criteria: rank stability evaluates whether the rank-correlation trajectory has reached a structural plateau, while structural sufficiency evaluates whether the spread of citation shares among established domains -- those whose confidence intervals exclude zero -- exceeds the uncertainty of those estimates. Together, these criteria distinguish rankings that have merely stabilized from those sufficiently resolved to support

translated_title: 从随机到稳定：AI可见性测量中的排名稳定性与结构充分性
translated_abstract: AI可见性测量具有比较性：从业者希望知道生成搜索引擎最常引用哪些领域，以及观察到的差异是否足够大以支持决策。然而，行业缺乏一种原则性的方法来确定是否已收集到足够的数据。不同研究和平台之间的收集预算差异很大，结论往往基于稳定性和精度未知的排名得出。我们引入了一个基于两个互补标准的序贯收敛框架：排名稳定性评估秩相关轨迹是否已达到结构平台期，而结构充分性评估既定领域（那些置信区间排除零的领域）之间的引用份额分布是否超过了这些估计的不确定性。这两个标准共同区分了仅仅稳定的排名与足以支持决策的充分解析排名。
tldr: 本文提出了一种结合排名稳定性与结构充分性的序贯收敛框架，用于判断AI可见性测量中数据收集是否充分，从而区分稳定但不足的排名与足以支持决策的排名。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a sequential convergence framework combining rank stability and structural sufficiency to determine data sufficiency in AI visibility measurement, distinguishing merely stable rankings from those sufficiently resolved for decision-making.
